title: Mini Quiz Functions
story: Your little sibling needs to practice spelling and math. Instead of quizzing them manually every day, you build a reusable quiz engine — one function that fires questions and checks answers automatically.
why: A single quiz function called repeatedly with different arguments demonstrates how parameterized functions eliminate duplicated logic.
analogy: A quiz function is like a Scantron grading machine. Each student bubble sheet (call) passes through the same machine (function) with different answer keys (parameters). The machine doesn't care what subject the test is about — it just compares answers to the key.
try_it: Modify `ask_question` to accept two wrong answer options and print them alongside the correct answer, simulating a multiple-choice quiz. Track the score across 5 questions.
tips: A Bool-returning function can be used directly in an if statement: `if ask_question(...) { }`
Each call to ask_question is independent — they don't affect each other
Score tracking happens in main(), not inside the function — the function just checks
common_mistakes: Hardcoding the answer inside the function instead of passing it as a parameter
Forgetting to increment score when the answer is correct
Using `=` instead of `==` for comparison inside the function
